Two terror operatives involved in funneling millions of shekels to Hamas were killed in strikes in the Gaza Strip last week, the military says.

The IDF says one strike on Wednesday in Gaza City killed Alaa Ibrahim Nimer Arshi, a cell commander in Hamas's military wing, and a strike on Tuesday in Nuseirat killed Karam Riyad Hassan Abu Butaihan, a Palestinian Islamic Jihad operative.

Both operatives were involved in transferring millions of shekels from Iran and Turkey to Hamas's military wing, according to the military.

"Recently, these funds helped the organization in its attempts to rebuild its military capabilities and advance terror attacks against IDF troops and Israeli civilians, in systematic violation of the ceasefire," the military says, adding that the "terrorists were killed in airstrikes to eliminate the threat."

Separately, the IDF says it bombed three Hamas weapon depots in the central Gaza Strip on Thursday.

The sites had been used by Hamas to store various weapons, including Kalashnikov rifles, rockets, and a rocket launcher, the military adds.

Defense Minister Israel Katz denies reports of a major confrontation between Israel's political leadership and IDF Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir, adding that Israel had no plans to strike Iran before the elections.

"The reports of disagreements between the political leadership and the IDF on Iran are completely baseless and false," Katz says in a statement.

Last night, Channel 12 news reported that a clash between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Zamir centered on an instruction by the prime minister for unspecified military action that defense officials believe could lead to a swift confrontation with Iran shortly before the election.

Army Radio published similar details this morning, citing two senior security officials.

"I state unequivocally that Israel had no intention of initiating an attack on Iran before the elections in Israel, while making clear that if Iran attacks Israel, we will respond with great force," Katz says, adding that "all reports on this matter are completely false."

The final voter turnout in Israel's national elections among IDF soldiers reached 79.9%, the military says.

The IDF says this is an increase of 6.2% compared to the previous elections in 2022.

Conscripts, career soldiers, and reservists began voting a week ago at over 890 polling stations deployed to military bases across the country and beyond Israel's borders, including at army posts in the Gaza Strip, Lebanon, and Syria.

An Israeli soldier has been arrested and charged with carrying out a slew of espionage tasks on behalf of Iran in exchange for cryptocurrency, authorities announce.

The soldier had been arrested in September following a joint investigation carried out by the Shin Bet, Israel Police, and Military Police, which suspected him of committing "grave security offenses, including maintaining contact with Iranian intelligence operatives and carrying out tasks under their direction."

Today, military prosecutors filed an indictment charging him with passing information to the enemy with the intent to harm state security and for the benefit of the enemy, as well as contact with a foreign agent.

The Shin Bet, police, and IDF say that during his interrogation, it emerged that the soldier had maintained contact with Iranian agents for about a year, during which he provided sensitive information about his unit's military activities, the IDF's readiness and call-ups, including details about his own call-up at the outbreak of the war with Iran earlier this year.

Four Hamas operatives were killed in strikes in the southern Gaza Strip on Wednesday, the military announces.

One strike in Khan Younis killed Mohammed Alyan al-Bayouk, identified by the IDF as a member of Hamas's elite Nukhba Force.

The Saudi newspaper Asharq Al-Awsat reported earlier that the Shin Bet security agency called Bayouk before carrying out the strike, telling him he had to choose between being killed alongside his family or being killed alone on the roof. According to the report, Bayouk chose to go up to the roof, where he was killed.

Iran's regime is so desperate for cash it's printing increasingly worthless rials just to avoid missing payroll for its security forces, government workers, and pensioners.

At 2.72 million rials to the dollar, the regime can print salaries. It can't print purchasing power.

اما وقتی پول ملی فروپاشیده، چاپ پول با پرداخت حقوق یکی نیست.

با دلار ۲.۷۲ میلیون ریالی، حکومت می‌تواند حقوق چاپ کند، ولی قدرت خرید نه.
